text: For a zero-input ESN in the large-N limit the maximal Lyapunov exponent is lambda_max = ln rho(W_rec) + <ln|tanh'|>. Near rho = 1 with small inputs this implies:
choices: lambda_max diverges to +infinity, so the reservoir is always chaotic
lambda_max ~ ln rho, so the edge of chaos (lambda_max = 0) coincides with rho ~ 1
lambda_max ~ -rho, so larger rho always means faster forgetting
lambda_max is independent of rho and set only by the input scaling
explanation: With small inputs |tanh'| ~ 1 so <ln|tanh'|> ~ 0, leaving lambda_max ~ ln rho(W_rec). The critical point lambda_max = 0 (edge of chaos, perturbations neither grow nor decay) then falls exactly at rho = 1, reproducing the spectral-radius rule. lambda_max stays finite, larger rho gives lambda_max closer to 0 (slower, not faster forgetting), and it clearly depends on rho, ruling out the other options.
